Zahruha riyat, wa waraquha burud, wa qidabuha ʿanbar, wa baṭḥaʾuha yaqut, wa turabuha kafur, wa ḥamluha misk, yakhruju min asliha anhar al-khamr wa al-laban wa al-ʿasal. Wa hiya majlis li-ahl al-Jannah, fa-baynama hum fi majlisihim idha atathum al-malaʾika min rabbihim yaqudun lijamaha, mazmuma bi-salasil min dhahab, wujuhuha ka-l-masabih husnan, wa wabruha ka-khazz al-marʿazi min layyina, ʿalayha rihal alwahuha min yaqut wa dafufuha min dhahab wa thiyabuha min sundusin wa istabraq. Fa-yaftaḥunaha wa yaqulun: inna rabbana arsalana ilaykum li-tazuruhu wa tusallimu ʿalayhi.

Qal: Fa-yarkabunaha fa-hiya asraʿu min al-ṭaʾir wa awṭaʾu min al-firash, najaban min ghayr mahna. Yasiru al-rajul ila janb akhihi wa huwa yukallimuhu wa yunajihi, la tuṣibu udhnu rahila minha idhna ṣāḥibatiha. Ḥatta inna al-shajara li-tantahi ʿan ṭuruqihim, fa-hum la yufarriquna bayn al-rajul wa bayn akhihi. Qal: Fa-yatuna ila al-Rahman al-Rahim fa-yusfiru lahum ʿan wajhihi al-karim, ḥatta yanẓuru ilayhi. Fa-idha ra'awhu qalu: "Allahumma anta al-Salam wa minka al-Salam, wa anta al-Jalal wa al-Ikram." Wa yaqulu tabaraka wa taʿala ʿinda dhalika: "Ana al-Salam wa minni al-Salam, wa ʿalaykum ḥaqqat raḥmati wa maḥabbati. Marḥaban bi-ʿibadi alladhina khashawni bi-l-ghayb wa aṭaʿu amri." Qal: Fa-yaqulun: "Rabbana lam naʿbudka ḥaqqa ʿibadatika wa lam naqdirka ḥaqqa qadrika, fa-adhan lana fi al-sujud qudamaka." Qal: Fa-yaqulu Allah ʿazza wa jalla: "Innaha laysat bi-dar nasab wa ʿibada, wa lakinna dar mulk wa naʿim, wa inni qad rafaʿtu ʿankum nasab al-ʿibada, fa-salūnī ma shi'tum, fa-inna li-kull rajul minkum umniyatahu." Fa-yasʾaluhu ḥatta inna aqṣarahum umniyatan yaqulu: "Rabbi, yatanafasu ahl al-dunya fi dunyahum fa-taḍayaqū fīha, fa-ataniya mithl kull shayʾin kanu fihi min yawm khalaqtaha ila an intahat." Fa-yaqulu Allah ʿazza wa jalla: "Laqad qaṣarat bika umniyatuka, wa laqad saʾalta dūna manzilatika, hadha laka minni, wa sa-alḥiquka bi-man ata, li-annahu laysa fi ʿaṭāʾī takdīr wa la taṣdīr."

Qal: Thumma yaqulu: "Aʿriḍū ʿalā ʿibadī mā lam tablugh umniyatuhum wa lam yakhṭur lahum ʿalā bāl," fa-yaʿriḍūna ʿalayhim ḥatta taqṣura bihim amāniyyuhum allatī fī anfusihim, fa-yakūnu fīmā yaʿriḍūna ʿalayhim barādhīn muqarrana ʿalā kull arbaʿa minhum sarīr min yāqūta wāḥida, ʿalā kull sarīr minhā qubba min dhahab mufraghah. Fī kull qubba minhā furush min furush al-Jannah muẓāhara, fī kull qubba minhā jāriyatān min al-Ḥūr al-ʿĪn, wa ʿalā kull jāriya minhunna thawbān min thiyāb al-Jannah. Wa laysa fi al-Jannati lawn illa wa huwa fīhimā, wa lā rīḥ ṭayyib illā wa qad ʿabiqa bihimā. Yanfudhu ḍawʾ wujūhihimā ghilaẓ al-qubba ḥatta yaẓunnu man yarāhumā annahumā dūna al-qubba, yurā mukhhumā min fawq saqfihimā, ka-l-silk al-abyaḍ min yāqūta ḥamrāʾ.

Yarayāni lahu min al-faḍl ʿalā ṣāḥibatihi ka-faḍl al-shams ʿalā al-ḥijāra aw afḍal, wa yarā huwa lahumā mithl dhalika. Thumma yadkhulu ilayhimā fa-yuṭayyibānihi wa yuqabbilānihi wa yuʿāniqānihi, wa yaqūlāni lahu: "Wallahi ma ẓanannā anna Allah yakhluqu mithlaka." [[Fī al-maṣdar: fa-yuḥayyiyānihi wa yuqabbilānihi wa yatarallaqāni bihi.]] Thumma yaʾmuru Allah al-malaʾika fayasīrūna bihim ṣaffan fī al-Jannah ḥatta yantahiya kull rajul minhum ila manzilatihi allatī uʿiddat lahu. [[Bi-ṭūlihi fī Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 3/533, wa Tafsir al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/60.]]

Al-Kalbi ʿan Abi Salih ʿan Ibn ʿAbbas: "Fa-Ṭūbā lahum" shajara aslaha fi dar ʿAlī fi al-Jannah, wa fi dar kull mu'min minha ghusn yuqalu lahu Ṭūbā.

"Wa ḥusnu maʾab": ḥusnu al-marjiʿ.

Wa rawā Dawud ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbar ʿan Jabir ʿan Abi Jaʿfar qal: su'ila Rasul Allah ﷺ ʿan qawlihi "Ṭūbā lahum wa ḥusnu maʾab." Faqal: "Shajara aslaha fi dari wa farʿuha fi al-Jannah." Thumma su'ila ʿanha marratan ukhra, faqal: "Shajara fi al-Jannah aslaha fi dar ʿAlī wa farʿuha ʿala ahl al-Jannah." Faqila lahu: "Ya Rasul Allah, nas'aluka ʿanha marra, faqulta: 'Shajara fi al-Jannah aslaha fi dar ʿAlī wa farʿuha ʿala ahl al-Jannah'," faqal: "Dhalika fi dari wa dar ʿAlī aydan wahida fi makan wahid." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 9/317, wa al-ʿUmda ʿan al-Tha'labi: 351.]]

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 13, verses 15–29 (part 1 of 2):

﴿And to Allah prostrate whoever is in the heavens and the earth,﴾ meaning the angels and the believers, ﴿willingly and unwillingly﴾ meaning the hypocrites and the disbelievers who were compelled to prostrate with the sword.

Ibn al-Mubarak narrated from Sufyan, who said: "Rabi' ibn Hushaym, whenever he recited this verse, would say: 'Nay, willingly, O my Lord!'"

﴿and their shadows at morning and evening﴾ meaning the shadows of those who prostrate, willingly or unwillingly. Their shadow prostrates to Allah when it inclines from their right or left.

Ibn 'Abbas said: "Its parallel is in al-Nahl (surah 16)."

al-Kalbi said: "When he prostrates at morning or evening, his shadow prostrates with him."

Mujahid said: "The shadow of the believer prostrates willingly, as he is obedient, and the shadow of the disbeliever prostrates willingly while he is unwilling." ﴿al-asal﴾ is the plural of ﴿asil﴾, and ﴿al-asil﴾ is the period from the afternoon ('asr) until sunset.

﴿Say: Who is the Lord of the heavens and the earth?﴾ That is, their Creator and Manager. ﴿They will say: "Allah."﴾ They have no choice but to say this. When they answer you, ﴿say: "You too, say, Allah."﴾ Then, as a binding argument against them, it is said: ﴿Have you then taken, besides Him, protectors who do not possess for themselves any benefit or harm?﴾ meaning idols that they worship besides Allah, and which cannot possess for themselves any benefit or harm. Then the matter is put to them in another way: ﴿Say: Are the blind and the seeing equal?﴾ Likewise, the one who has strayed and the believer who is guided are not equal.

al-A'mash, 'Asim, Hamza and al-Kisa'i recited ﴿Am hal yastawi al-zulumat wa al-nur﴾ with the verb in the masculine (yastawi). The rest recited it with the feminine (tastawi). Abu 'Ubayd preferred this, saying: "Because it is joined to a feminine noun, and the verb is closer to the subject, and ﴿al-zulumat wa al-nur﴾ are like disbelief and faith."

﴿Or have they set up for Allah partners who created as He creates, so that the creation seemed similar to them?﴾ So they became unable to tell whether it was the creation of Allah or the creation of their gods. ﴿Say: Allah is the Creator of all things, and He is the One, the Subduer.﴾ [.........] [[An unreadable word.]] for truth and falsehood, two examples. Then the Mighty and Majestic One said: ﴿He sends down from the sky﴾ meaning rain, ﴿water, and valleys flow according to their measure﴾ large according to its measure and small according to its measure. ﴿So the torrent carries a foaming scum﴾ that arose from that flood, ﴿rising to the surface﴾ as the water is heated. The water that remains, pure and beneficial, is the truth. The scum that departs and vanishes, which clings to trees and the sides of valleys and rivers, is the falsehood. It is said: this is the flood of the Qur'an, which descends from the sky, and the hearts take from it their share according to their certainty and doubt, reason and ignorance. So this is the parable of truth and falsehood. [[Zad al-Masir: 4/237.]]

The other parable is His words: ﴿And from that which they kindle in the fire﴾.

Hamid Abu Mihjan, Abu Wahb and Hamza and al-Kisa'i recited ﴿yuqidun﴾ with the verb in the third person (yu-). Abu 'Ubayd preferred this, because of His words ﴿what benefits people﴾, and there is no address here. ﴿Seeking ornaments﴾ meaning adornment they make, ﴿or goods﴾ meaning what is benefited from; and everything one enjoys is a ﴿mata'﴾ (enjoyment).

al-Mash'ath said:
"Enjoy yourself, O Mash'ath, for whatever
you have been given before death is the enjoyment."
[[Tafsir al-Tabari: 13/180; Taj al-'Arus: 5/507.]]

By this he meant the precious things of the earth, gold and silver, ﴿iron, brass, copper and lead﴾, and from them one extracts things that benefit, such as ornaments, vessels and others.

﴿A scum like it.﴾ He says: it has a scum, when the feminine is used, like the scum of the flood. What remains pure from these precious things is what remains, and its dross departs, and the scum that does not remain and is not beneficial is like falsehood.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Thus Allah sets forth truth and falsehood. As for the scum, it passes away as worthless.﴾ ﴿Then the scum that rose over the flood will depart as foam, scattered quickly.﴾ Abu 'Amr said: it comes from the saying of the Arabs: "ajfa'at al-qidr al-nidhr wa jannat," which means when it boils and its scum overflows, or when it settles, nothing of it remains. [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 13/180.]]

al-Qutabi said: "al-jifa' is what the valley throws out to its banks." Then he said: "jafa'tuhu" means "I knocked him down."

Ibn al-Anbari said: "jifa'" means "scattered, perished."

It is said: "jafa'at al-rih bi al-ghaym" when the wind scatters the clouds and carries them away.

Some of them said: it means the earth's separation. It is said: "jafa'a al-wadi" and "ajfa'a" when it dried up.

al-Farra' said: "He only meant by His words jufa'an (as foam) the jifa', because it is a verbal noun. Your saying: 'jafa'a al-wadi ghathauhu jifa'an' (the valley cast out its scum as foam) came out in the form of a noun, though it is a verbal noun." The Arabs do the same with the verbal noun of every verb where a thing gathers part to part, such as ﴿qamash﴾ (miscellany), ﴿raqaq﴾ (rags), ﴿hutam﴾ (debris) and ﴿ghunam﴾ (spoils); they bring it out in the manner of a noun, as in their saying: "a'taytuhu 'ata'an" in the sense of "i'ta'" (giving). Had they intended the verbal noun in its proper form for qamash, they would say: "qammashtuhu qamashan."

﴿As for that which benefits people, it remains in the earth.﴾ ﴿Thus Allah sets forth the parables.﴾ The speech on this is complete. Then He said: ﴿For those who responded to their Lord, the best reward.﴾ That is, obeyed Him: the good in Paradise. ﴿And those who did not respond to Him, even if they had all that is in the earth and the like of it with it, they would surely offer it as ransom on the Day of Resurrection.﴾ Allah said: ﴿For those is the evil reckoning﴾, requiting them with punishment. Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said, and the scum: "Do you know what the evil reckoning is?"
I said: "No."
He said: "It is that a man is called to account for a sin he committed, and his sin is not forgiven."

﴿And their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the resting place﴾ meaning the bed and the destination.

﴿Is then one who knows that what has been sent down to you from your Lord is the truth [.........] [[An unreadable word.]]﴾ so he is sufficient, ﴿like one who is blind to it﴾, who does not know it and does not act upon it? ﴿Only those of understanding remember﴾. The address is to the companions and the people of reason, ﴿who fulfill the covenant of Allah﴾ in their affairs, meaning His obligation upon them, so they do not oppose it for that in which they are, ﴿and do not break the pact﴾, ﴿and those who join what Allah has commanded to be joined﴾. It was said: He meant faith in all the books and messengers, and they do not disbelieve in them.

Most of the exegetes said: it means the kinship ties (rahm), and they sever them.

al-Zuhri, from Abu Salama ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, said: "Abu al-Darda' fell ill, and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf visited him. He said: 'Choose for them the one who joins them, as far as you know, O Muhammad.' 'Abd al-Rahman said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Allah, blessed and exalted, said: I am Allah and I am the Merciful. I created the womb and derived for it a name from My name. Whoever joins it, I join him, and whoever severs it, I sever him.'" [141] [[Musnad Ahmad: 1/194, where it reads "battatahu" in place of "qata'atahu"; the full text is in Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 1/104.]]

From Shayba, who said: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Mawhab and his father 'Uthman ibn 'Abd Allah told us that they both heard Musa ibn Talha narrate from Abu Ayyub al-Ansari: that a man said: "O Messenger of Allah, inform me of a deed that will admit me to Paradise." The people said: "What is wrong with him? What is wrong with him?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "He has a need." Then the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "You worship Allah, associating nothing with Him, establish the prayer, give the zakat, and join the ties of kinship, leave it." He said: as if he was on his mount. [142] [[Sahih Ibn Hibban: 8/38.]]

From 'Ata' ibn Abi Marwan, from his father, from Ka'b, who said: "By the One who split the sea for the Children of Israel, indeed in the Torah it is written: 'O son of Adam, fear your Lord, be dutiful to your parents, join your kinship ties; I will lengthen your life for you, make your ease easy for you, and turn away your hardship from you.'" [[Al-Musannaf of Ibn Abi Shayba: 6/97.]]

And from Abu Ishaq, from Mughra' al-'Abdi, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: "Whoever fears his Lord and joins his kinship ties, his life will be extended, his wealth will increase, and his family will love him." [[Al-Adab al-Mufrad: 24.]]

From Salih, from Jarir, from Burd, from Makhul, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do good [there is no act of obedience to Allah more quickly rewarded than joining kinship ties], and there is nothing more quickly punished than oppression and severing kinship ties, and a false oath leaves homes desolate." [143] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 3/368; al-Jami' al-Saghir: 2/455.]]

﴿And those who are patient﴾ in obedience to Allah and restrain themselves from disobedience to Allah. This was said by Ibn Zayd. Ibn 'Abbas said: "And they were patient in the command of Allah." 'Ata' said: "In calamities, misfortunes, accidents and trials." Abu 'Imran al-Juni said: "They were patient in their religion."

﴿Seeking the face of Allah﴾, a seeker who holds fast to Allah and asks his Lord for forgiveness that he might disobey Him or oppose His command, ﴿and establish the prayer, and spend of what We have provided them, secretly and openly﴾, meaning the zakat. ﴿And they repel with good the evil﴾ meaning they push it away. It is said: "daraa Allah 'anni bi-sharrika" (Allah has warded off your evil from me).

Ibn Zayd said: that is, they do not repay evil with evil, but repel it with good.

al-Qutabi said: its meaning is that when they are insulted, they show forbearance; the insult is the evil and the forbearance is the good.

Qatada said: they return kindness to those who wrong them. Its parallel is: ﴿When the ignorant address them, they say, "Peace."﴾ [[Surat al-Furqan: 63.]]

al-Hasan said: when they are denied, they give; when they are wronged, they pardon; and when they are severed, they join.

Ibn Kaysan said: when they sin, they despair; and when they transgress, they are rewarded, so that by repentance they ward off from themselves, and the sin is forgiven.

This is the statement of Ibn 'Abbas in the narration of al-Dahhak from him, who said: "They repel evil deeds with righteous deeds." This is supported by the reported hadith: Mu'adh ibn Jabal said: "O Messenger of Allah, advise me." He said: "When you do an evil deed, follow it with a good deed to erase it: secret with secret, and open with open." [144] [[Majma' al-Zawa'id: 4/218.]]

'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak said: "These are eight qualities, indicating the eight gates of Paradise."

Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: "These are eight bridges; whoever wishes nearness to Allah must cross them." [[Tafsir al-Tha'alibi: 3/367.]]

﴿Those will have the good final home﴾. Then He explained, saying: ﴿Gardens of perpetual residence which they will enter.﴾

The common readers recited it with a fatha on the ya' and a damma on the kha' (yadkhulunaha). Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr recited it with a damma on the ya' and a fatha on the kha' (yudkhalunaha).

'Abd Allah ibn 'Umayr said: "In Paradise there is a palace called 'Adn, around which are towers and meadows. It has five thousand doors, and at each door are five thousand brides. Only a prophet, a truthful one, or a martyr enters it." [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 15/834; Tafsir al-Tabari: 10/232.]] [[In al-Tabari: "al-rawh" (the meadows); in Majma' al-Zawa'id (5/196): "al-suruh" (the palaces).]]

﴿And whoever is righteous among their fathers, their spouses and their offspring﴾, meaning their families and children also, will enter it. ﴿And the angels will enter upon them from every gate, saying: "Peace be upon you, for that which you patiently endured. And excellent is the final home."﴾ It was said: they are secure therein. The implied sense is: and they say, "Peace be upon you."

Muqatil said: they enter, within the span of a day and night of the days of this world, three times, bringing gifts and presents, saying: "Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured."

From Salih, from Yazid, from Anas ibn Malik: that he recited this verse, "Gardens of perpetual residence" up to His words, "excellent is the final home."

Then he said: It is a Paradise of gold and silver, its height in the air is sixty miles, with no crack or joint in it. Each corner of it has its people. It has four thousand leaves of gold, and at each door stand seventy thousand angels, and with each angel is a gift from the Most Merciful, the like of which does not exist. [.........] [[An unreadable word.]] there is no veil between them and Him.

Ibn al-Mubarak narrated from 'Uqba ibn al-Walid, who said: Artat ibn al-Mundhir told us: I heard a man from Mulajlaj bi-al-Jund, called Abu al-Hajjaj, say: My maternal uncle, Abu Umama, told me: "Indeed the believer, when he enters Paradise, reclines on his couch, and at his side are two rows of servants, and at the end of the two rows is a wall. An angel comes and asks permission. The one nearest to him says: 'An angel asks permission,' and the one next to him says: 'An angel asks permission,' and so on until it reaches the believer, who says: 'Let him in.' The one nearest to the believer says: 'Let him in,' and the one next to him says the same to the one beside him, until it reaches the farthest of them at the door. It is opened for him, and he enters, greets, and then departs." [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 13/186.]]

From 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do you know who will be the first of Allah's creation to enter Paradise?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "The poor and the emigrants, through whom the frontiers are guarded and hardships are averted, and one of them dies with a need in his heart that he cannot fulfill." [145] [[Musnad Ahmad: 2/168.]]

He said: Then the angels come to them: ﴿They enter upon them from every gate, saying: "Peace be upon you, for that which you patiently endured."﴾

Sahl ibn Abi Salih narrated from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) used to visit the graves of the martyrs at the beginning of every year, saying: "Peace be upon you for that which you patiently endured; and excellent is the final home."

Abu Bakr, 'Umar and 'Uthman (peace be upon them) used to do the same.

﴿And those who break the covenant of Allah after its ratification, and sever what Allah has commanded to be joined, and cause corruption in the earth, for them is the curse, and for them is the evil abode﴾, meaning the Fire.

Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas said: "They are the Harurites (Kharijites)."

﴿Allah extends provision to whom He wills, and restricts it﴾, meaning He widens it for whom He wills, ﴿and constricts﴾ and straitens. ﴿And they rejoiced in the life of this world﴾, meaning they neglected and were ignorant of what is with Allah, and they coveted. ﴿And the life of this world, in the Hereafter, is but a little enjoyment﴾, a small and passing thing. This was said by Mujahid. 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabit said: "Like the provision of a shepherd who takes with him a handful of dates, or some flour, or something over which he drinks milk." [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 13/189.]]

al-Kalbi said: "Like a small bowl, a dish, a cup, a pot, and the like, from which one benefits and then it passes away."

﴿And those who disbelieve, from the people of Makkah, say: "Why has a sign not been sent down upon him from his Lord?"﴾ Say: ﴿Indeed, Allah misguides whom He wills and guides to Himself whoever turns back﴾, guiding the community to His obedience, the one who returns to Him with his heart. Then He described them, saying: ﴿Those who believe﴾ in the place of accusative, and the preceding "alladhina" is in the nominative. ﴿And their hearts find rest in the remembrance of Allah.﴾

Muqatil said: "With the Qur'an." ﴿Unquestionably, by the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest.﴾

Ibn 'Abbas said: "This is about oaths: when a Muslim swears by Allah about something, that is what calms the hearts of the believers toward it."

Mujahid said: "They are the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)."

﴿Those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them is Tuba (bliss)﴾, a beginning, and its predicate follows. It was said: its meaning is "for them is Tuba," so "Tuba" is the predicate of the first subject.

The scholars differed in interpreting "Tuba."

al-Walibi reported from Ibn 'Abbas: "Tuba lahum": joy and comfort of the eye for them. 'Ikrima said: "How good is what they have." al-Dahhak said: "Enviable state for them." Qatada said: "Beautiful state for them." Ma'mar reported from him: "This is an Arabic expression; a man says to another, 'Tuba lakum,' meaning you have obtained good." Ibrahim said: "Goodness and honor for them." Shumayt ibn 'Ajlan said: "Tuba means the continuance of good." al-Farra' said: "It derives from goodness, and the waw came because of the preceding damma, and it is from the speech of the Arabs: 'Tubaka, tuba laka.'" Sa'id ibn Jubayr reported from Ibn 'Abbas: "Tuba is the name of Paradise in Abyssinian." Sa'id ibn Masjuh said: "It is the name of Paradise in Hindi; the 'spring of the garden' in the language of India." [[Cf. Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 2/53.]]

Ibn Sa'id al-Hindi narrated from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that a man said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, what is Tuba?" He said: "A tree in Paradise, whose length is a hundred years; the garments of the people of Paradise come out of its sheaths." [146] [[Musnad Ahmad: 3/71.]]

Mu'awiya ibn Murra narrated from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Tuba is a tree which Allah planted with His hand and breathed into it of His spirit. It brings forth ornaments and garments, and its branches can be seen from beyond the wall of Paradise." [147] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 14/357, no. 39250.]]

Abu Hurayra said: "Tuba is a tree in Paradise, which Allah planted for it; its fruit ... for My servant 'Ayyash, prepared for him from ornaments, with its saddle and its flesh, and from camels, beneath which is cloth of garments."

Mughith ibn Sumayy said: "Tuba is a tree of Paradise. If a man rode a young she-camel and then went around with her, he would not reach the place from which he set out until he died of old age. There is not a household but has in it a branch of that tree hanging down, the water reaching them by buckets. When they wish to eat from the fruit, it lowers itself to them, and they eat from it what they wish. Birds like camels come upon it, and they eat from it roasted and cooked meat, and then they fly off." [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 13/195.]]

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 13, verse 15–29 (part 2 of 2):

Qal ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr: hiya shajara fi Jannat ʿAdn, asluha fi dar al-Nabi ﷺ, wa fi kull dar wa ghurfa ghusn minha. Lam yakhluq Allah lawnan wa la zahra illa wa fiha minha, illa al-sawad, wa lam yakhluq Allah fakiha wa la thamara illa wa fiha minha. Yanbaʿu min asliha ʿaynan: al-Kafur wa al-Salsabil. Muqabil kull waraqa minha tuzallu umma ʿalayha, ʿalayha malak yusabbihu Allah bi-anwaʿ al-tasbih. [[Al-ʿUmda ʿan al-Tha'labi: 351, wa Fath al-Qadir: 4/373 ḥ 5312.]]

Wa qal Abu Salam: ḥaddathani ʿAmir ibn Zayd al-Bakali annahu samiʿa ʿUtba ibn ʿUbayd al-Sulami yaqulu: jaʾa aʿrabi ila al-Nabi ﷺ fa-qal: "Ya Rasul Allah, fi al-Janna fakiha?" Qal: "Fiha shajara tudʿa Tuba, hiya tutabiqu al-Firdaws." [[Al-Muʿjam al-Kabir: 17/127, Jamiʿ al-Bayan li-l-Tabari: 13/195.]]

Qal: "Ayy shajar ardina tushabih?" Qal: "Laysa tushabihu shayʾan min shajar ardika, wa lakin atayta al-Sham." Faqal: "Atayta al-Sham ya Rasul Allah ﷺ?" Qal: "Fa-innaha tushabihu shajara tudʿa al-Jawz, tanbutu ʿala saqin wahid thumma yantashiru aʿlaha." Faqal: "Ma aʿzama asliha!"

Qal: "Law irtahalat jadʿa min ibil ahlika ma ahatat bi-asliha hatta tankasira tarquwatahuma harman." [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 13/195.]]

Qal Wahb ibn Munabbih: inna fi al-Jannati shajara. Qal: al-Tuba yasiru al-rakib fi zillaha miʾata ʿam wa la yaqtaʿuha. Zahruha riyat, wa waraquha burud, wa qidabuha ʿanbar, wa baṭḥaʾuha yaqut, wa turabuha kafur, wa ḥamluha misk, yakhruju min asliha anhar al-khamr wa al-laban wa al-ʿasal. Wa hiya majlis li-ahl al-Jannah, fa-baynama hum fi majlisihim idha atathum al-malaʾika min rabbihim yaqudun lijamaha, mazmuma bi-salasil min dhahab, wujuhuha ka-l-masabih husnan, wa wabruha ka-khazz al-marʿazi min layyina, ʿalayha rihal alwahuha min yaqut wa dafufuha min dhahab wa thiyabuha min sundusin wa istabraq. Fa-yaftaḥunaha wa yaqulun: inna rabbana arsalana ilaykum li-tazuruhu wa tusallimu ʿalayhi.

Qal: Fa-yarkabunaha fa-hiya asraʿu min al-ṭaʾir wa awṭaʾu min al-firash, najaban min ghayr mahna. Yasiru al-rajul ila janb akhihi wa huwa yukallimuhu wa yunajihi, la tuṣibu udhnu rahila minha idhna ṣāḥibatiha. Ḥatta inna al-shajara li-tantahi ʿan ṭuruqihim, fa-hum la yufarriquna bayn al-rajul wa bayn akhihi. Qal: Fa-yatuna ila al-Rahman al-Rahim fa-yusfiru lahum ʿan wajhihi al-karim, ḥatta yanẓuru ilayhi. Fa-idha ra'awhu qalu: "Allahumma anta al-Salam wa minka al-Salam, wa anta al-Jalal wa al-Ikram." Wa yaqulu tabaraka wa taʿala ʿinda dhalika: "Ana al-Salam wa minni al-Salam, wa ʿalaykum ḥaqqat raḥmati wa maḥabbati. Marḥaban bi-ʿibadi alladhina khashawni bi-l-ghayb wa aṭaʿu amri." Qal: Fa-yaqulun: "Rabbana lam naʿbudka ḥaqqa ʿibadatika wa lam naqdirka ḥaqqa qadrika, fa-adhan lana fi al-sujud qudamaka." Qal: Fa-yaqulu Allah ʿazza wa jalla: "Innaha laysat bi-dar nasab wa ʿibada, wa lakinna dar mulk wa naʿim, wa inni qad rafaʿtu ʿankum nasab al-ʿibada, fa-salūnī ma shi'tum, fa-inna li-kull rajul minkum umniyatahu." Fa-yasʾaluhu ḥatta inna aqṣarahum umniyatan yaqulu: "Rabbi, yatanafasu ahl al-dunya fi dunyahum fa-taḍayaqū fīha, fa-ataniya mithl kull shayʾin kanu fihi min yawm khalaqtaha ila an intahat." Fa-yaqulu Allah ʿazza wa jalla: "Laqad qaṣarat bika umniyatuka, wa laqad saʾalta dūna manzilatika, hadha laka minni, wa sa-alḥiquka bi-man ata, li-annahu laysa fi ʿaṭāʾī takdīr wa la taṣdīr."

Qal: Thumma yaqulu: "Aʿriḍū ʿalā ʿibadī mā lam tablugh umniyatuhum wa lam yakhṭur lahum ʿalā bāl," fa-yaʿriḍūna ʿalayhim ḥatta taqṣura bihim amāniyyuhum allatī fī anfusihim, fa-yakūnu fīmā yaʿriḍūna ʿalayhim barādhīn muqarrana ʿalā kull arbaʿa minhum sarīr min yāqūta wāḥida, ʿalā kull sarīr minhā qubba min dhahab mufraghah. Fī kull qubba minhā furush min furush al-Jannah muẓāhara, fī kull qubba minhā jāriyatān min al-Ḥūr al-ʿĪn, wa ʿalā kull jāriya minhunna thawbān min thiyāb al-Jannah. Wa laysa fi al-Jannati lawn illa wa huwa fīhimā, wa lā rīḥ ṭayyib illā wa qad ʿabiqa bihimā. Yanfudhu ḍawʾ wujūhihimā ghilaẓ al-qubba ḥatta yaẓunnu man yarāhumā annahumā dūna al-qubba, yurā mukhhumā min fawq saqfihimā, ka-l-silk al-abyaḍ min yāqūta ḥamrāʾ.

Yarayāni lahu min al-faḍl ʿalā ṣāḥibatihi ka-faḍl al-shams ʿalā al-ḥijāra aw afḍal, wa yarā huwa lahumā mithl dhalika. Thumma yadkhulu ilayhimā fa-yuṭayyibānihi wa yuqabbilānihi wa yuʿāniqānihi, wa yaqūlāni lahu: "Wallahi ma ẓanannā anna Allah yakhluqu mithlaka." [[Fī al-maṣdar: fa-yuḥayyiyānihi wa yuqabbilānihi wa yatarallaqāni bihi.]] Thumma yaʾmuru Allah al-malaʾika fayasīrūna bihim ṣaffan fī al-Jannah ḥatta yantahiya kull rajul minhum ila manzilatihi allatī uʿiddat lahu. [[Bi-ṭūlihi fī Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 3/533, wa Tafsir al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/60.]]

Al-Kalbi ʿan Abi Salih ʿan Ibn ʿAbbas: "Fa-Ṭūbā lahum" shajara aslaha fi dar ʿAlī fi al-Jannah, wa fi dar kull mu'min minha ghusn yuqalu lahu Ṭūbā.

"Wa ḥusnu maʾab": ḥusnu al-marjiʿ.

Wa rawā Dawud ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbar ʿan Jabir ʿan Abi Jaʿfar qal: su'ila Rasul Allah ﷺ ʿan qawlihi "Ṭūbā lahum wa ḥusnu maʾab." Faqal: "Shajara aslaha fi dari wa farʿuha fi al-Jannah." Thumma su'ila ʿanha marratan ukhra, faqal: "Shajara fi al-Jannah aslaha fi dar ʿAlī wa farʿuha ʿala ahl al-Jannah." Faqila lahu: "Ya Rasul Allah, nas'aluka ʿanha marra, faqulta: 'Shajara fi al-Jannah aslaha fi dar ʿAlī wa farʿuha ʿala ahl al-Jannah'," faqal: "Dhalika fi dari wa dar ʿAlī aydan wahida fi makan wahid." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 9/317, wa al-ʿUmda ʿan al-Tha'labi: 351.]]

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 13, verses 15–29 (part 1 of 2):

﴿And to Allah prostrate whoever is in the heavens and the earth,﴾ meaning the angels and the believers, ﴿willingly and unwillingly﴾ meaning the hypocrites and the disbelievers who were compelled to prostrate with the sword.

Ibn al-Mubarak narrated from Sufyan, who said: "Rabi' ibn Hushaym, whenever he recited this verse, would say: 'Nay, willingly, O my Lord!'"

﴿and their shadows at morning and evening﴾ meaning the shadows of those who prostrate, willingly or unwillingly. Their shadow prostrates to Allah when it inclines from their right or left.

Ibn 'Abbas said: "Its parallel is in al-Nahl (surah 16)."

al-Kalbi said: "When he prostrates at morning or evening, his shadow prostrates with him."

Mujahid said: "The shadow of the believer prostrates willingly, as he is obedient, and the shadow of the disbeliever prostrates willingly while he is unwilling." ﴿al-asal﴾ is the plural of ﴿asil﴾, and ﴿al-asil﴾ is the period from the afternoon ('asr) until sunset.

﴿Say: Who is the Lord of the heavens and the earth?﴾ That is, their Creator and Manager. ﴿They will say: "Allah."﴾ They have no choice but to say this. When they answer you, ﴿say: "You too, say, Allah."﴾ Then, as a binding argument against them, it is said: ﴿Have you then taken, besides Him, protectors who do not possess for themselves any benefit or harm?﴾ meaning idols that they worship besides Allah, and which cannot possess for themselves any benefit or harm. Then the matter is put to them in another way: ﴿Say: Are the blind and the seeing equal?﴾ Likewise, the one who has strayed and the believer who is guided are not equal.

al-A'mash, 'Asim, Hamza and al-Kisa'i recited ﴿Am hal yastawi al-zulumat wa al-nur﴾ with the verb in the masculine (yastawi). The rest recited it with the feminine (tastawi). Abu 'Ubayd preferred this, saying: "Because it is joined to a feminine noun, and the verb is closer to the subject, and ﴿al-zulumat wa al-nur﴾ are like disbelief and faith."

﴿Or have they set up for Allah partners who created as He creates, so that the creation seemed similar to them?﴾ So they became unable to tell whether it was the creation of Allah or the creation of their gods. ﴿Say: Allah is the Creator of all things, and He is the One, the Subduer.﴾ [.........] [[An unreadable word.]] for truth and falsehood, two examples. Then the Mighty and Majestic One said: ﴿He sends down from the sky﴾ meaning rain, ﴿water, and valleys flow according to their measure﴾ large according to its measure and small according to its measure. ﴿So the torrent carries a foaming scum﴾ that arose from that flood, ﴿rising to the surface﴾ as the water is heated. The water that remains, pure and beneficial, is the truth. The scum that departs and vanishes, which clings to trees and the sides of valleys and rivers, is the falsehood. It is said: this is the flood of the Qur'an, which descends from the sky, and the hearts take from it their share according to their certainty and doubt, reason and ignorance. So this is the parable of truth and falsehood. [[Zad al-Masir: 4/237.]]

The other parable is His words: ﴿And from that which they kindle in the fire﴾.

Hamid Abu Mihjan, Abu Wahb and Hamza and al-Kisa'i recited ﴿yuqidun﴾ with the verb in the third person (yu-). Abu 'Ubayd preferred this, because of His words ﴿what benefits people﴾, and there is no address here. ﴿Seeking ornaments﴾ meaning adornment they make, ﴿or goods﴾ meaning what is benefited from; and everything one enjoys is a ﴿mata'﴾ (enjoyment).

al-Mash'ath said:
"Enjoy yourself, O Mash'ath, for whatever
you have been given before death is the enjoyment."
[[Tafsir al-Tabari: 13/180; Taj al-'Arus: 5/507.]]

By this he meant the precious things of the earth, gold and silver, ﴿iron, brass, copper and lead﴾, and from them one extracts things that benefit, such as ornaments, vessels and others.

﴿A scum like it.﴾ He says: it has a scum, when the feminine is used, like the scum of the flood. What remains pure from these precious things is what remains, and its dross departs, and the scum that does not remain and is not beneficial is like falsehood.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Thus Allah sets forth truth and falsehood. As for the scum, it passes away as worthless.﴾ ﴿Then the scum that rose over the flood will depart as foam, scattered quickly.﴾ Abu 'Amr said: it comes from the saying of the Arabs: "ajfa'at al-qidr al-nidhr wa jannat," which means when it boils and its scum overflows, or when it settles, nothing of it remains. [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 13/180.]]

al-Qutabi said: "al-jifa' is what the valley throws out to its banks." Then he said: "jafa'tuhu" means "I knocked him down."

Ibn al-Anbari said: "jifa'" means "scattered, perished."

It is said: "jafa'at al-rih bi al-ghaym" when the wind scatters the clouds and carries them away.

Some of them said: it means the earth's separation. It is said: "jafa'a al-wadi" and "ajfa'a" when it dried up.

al-Farra' said: "He only meant by His words jufa'an (as foam) the jifa', because it is a verbal noun. Your saying: 'jafa'a al-wadi ghathauhu jifa'an' (the valley cast out its scum as foam) came out in the form of a noun, though it is a verbal noun." The Arabs do the same with the verbal noun of every verb where a thing gathers part to part, such as ﴿qamash﴾ (miscellany), ﴿raqaq﴾ (rags), ﴿hutam﴾ (debris) and ﴿ghunam﴾ (spoils); they bring it out in the manner of a noun, as in their saying: "a'taytuhu 'ata'an" in the sense of "i'ta'" (giving). Had they intended the verbal noun in its proper form for qamash, they would say: "qammashtuhu qamashan."

﴿As for that which benefits people, it remains in the earth.﴾ ﴿Thus Allah sets forth the parables.﴾ The speech on this is complete. Then He said: ﴿For those who responded to their Lord, the best reward.﴾ That is, obeyed Him: the good in Paradise. ﴿And those who did not respond to Him, even if they had all that is in the earth and the like of it with it, they would surely offer it as ransom on the Day of Resurrection.﴾ Allah said: ﴿For those is the evil reckoning﴾, requiting them with punishment. Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said, and the scum: "Do you know what the evil reckoning is?"
I said: "No."
He said: "It is that a man is called to account for a sin he committed, and his sin is not forgiven."

﴿And their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the resting place﴾ meaning the bed and the destination.

﴿Is then one who knows that what has been sent down to you from your Lord is the truth [.........] [[An unreadable word.]]﴾ so he is sufficient, ﴿like one who is blind to it﴾, who does not know it and does not act upon it? ﴿Only those of understanding remember﴾. The address is to the companions and the people of reason, ﴿who fulfill the covenant of Allah﴾ in their affairs, meaning His obligation upon them, so they do not oppose it for that in which they are, ﴿and do not break the pact﴾, ﴿and those who join what Allah has commanded to be joined﴾. It was said: He meant faith in all the books and messengers, and they do not disbelieve in them.

Most of the exegetes said: it means the kinship ties (rahm), and they sever them.

al-Zuhri, from Abu Salama ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, said: "Abu al-Darda' fell ill, and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf visited him. He said: 'Choose for them the one who joins them, as far as you know, O Muhammad.' 'Abd al-Rahman said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Allah, blessed and exalted, said: I am Allah and I am the Merciful. I created the womb and derived for it a name from My name. Whoever joins it, I join him, and whoever severs it, I sever him.'" [141] [[Musnad Ahmad: 1/194, where it reads "battatahu" in place of "qata'atahu"; the full text is in Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 1/104.]]

From Shayba, who said: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Mawhab and his father 'Uthman ibn 'Abd Allah told us that they both heard Musa ibn Talha narrate from Abu Ayyub al-Ansari: that a man said: "O Messenger of Allah, inform me of a deed that will admit me to Paradise." The people said: "What is wrong with him? What is wrong with him?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "He has a need." Then the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "You worship Allah, associating nothing with Him, establish the prayer, give the zakat, and join the ties of kinship, leave it." He said: as if he was on his mount. [142] [[Sahih Ibn Hibban: 8/38.]]

From 'Ata' ibn Abi Marwan, from his father, from Ka'b, who said: "By the One who split the sea for the Children of Israel, indeed in the Torah it is written: 'O son of Adam, fear your Lord, be dutiful to your parents, join your kinship ties; I will lengthen your life for you, make your ease easy for you, and turn away your hardship from you.'" [[Al-Musannaf of Ibn Abi Shayba: 6/97.]]

And from Abu Ishaq, from Mughra' al-'Abdi, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: "Whoever fears his Lord and joins his kinship ties, his life will be extended, his wealth will increase, and his family will love him." [[Al-Adab al-Mufrad: 24.]]

From Salih, from Jarir, from Burd, from Makhul, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do good [there is no act of obedience to Allah more quickly rewarded than joining kinship ties], and there is nothing more quickly punished than oppression and severing kinship ties, and a false oath leaves homes desolate." [143] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 3/368; al-Jami' al-Saghir: 2/455.]]

﴿And those who are patient﴾ in obedience to Allah and restrain themselves from disobedience to Allah. This was said by Ibn Zayd. Ibn 'Abbas said: "And they were patient in the command of Allah." 'Ata' said: "In calamities, misfortunes, accidents and trials." Abu 'Imran al-Juni said: "They were patient in their religion."

﴿Seeking the face of Allah﴾, a seeker who holds fast to Allah and asks his Lord for forgiveness that he might disobey Him or oppose His command, ﴿and establish the prayer, and spend of what We have provided them, secretly and openly﴾, meaning the zakat. ﴿And they repel with good the evil﴾ meaning they push it away. It is said: "daraa Allah 'anni bi-sharrika" (Allah has warded off your evil from me).

Ibn Zayd said: that is, they do not repay evil with evil, but repel it with good.

al-Qutabi said: its meaning is that when they are insulted, they show forbearance; the insult is the evil and the forbearance is the good.

Qatada said: they return kindness to those who wrong them. Its parallel is: ﴿When the ignorant address them, they say, "Peace."﴾ [[Surat al-Furqan: 63.]]

al-Hasan said: when they are denied, they give; when they are wronged, they pardon; and when they are severed, they join.

Ibn Kaysan said: when they sin, they despair; and when they transgress, they are rewarded, so that by repentance they ward off from themselves, and the sin is forgiven.

This is the statement of Ibn 'Abbas in the narration of al-Dahhak from him, who said: "They repel evil deeds with righteous deeds." This is supported by the reported hadith: Mu'adh ibn Jabal said: "O Messenger of Allah, advise me." He said: "When you do an evil deed, follow it with a good deed to erase it: secret with secret, and open with open." [144] [[Majma' al-Zawa'id: 4/218.]]

'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak said: "These are eight qualities, indicating the eight gates of Paradise."

Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: "These are eight bridges; whoever wishes nearness to Allah must cross them." [[Tafsir al-Tha'alibi: 3/367.]]

﴿Those will have the good final home﴾. Then He explained, saying: ﴿Gardens of perpetual residence which they will enter.﴾

The common readers recited it with a fatha on the ya' and a damma on the kha' (yadkhulunaha). Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr recited it with a damma on the ya' and a fatha on the kha' (yudkhalunaha).

'Abd Allah ibn 'Umayr said: "In Paradise there is a palace called 'Adn, around which are towers and meadows. It has five thousand doors, and at each door are five thousand brides. Only a prophet, a truthful one, or a martyr enters it." [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 15/834; Tafsir al-Tabari: 10/232.]] [[In al-Tabari: "al-rawh" (the meadows); in Majma' al-Zawa'id (5/196): "al-suruh" (the palaces).]]

﴿And whoever is righteous among their fathers, their spouses and their offspring﴾, meaning their families and children also, will enter it. ﴿And the angels will enter upon them from every gate, saying: "Peace be upon you, for that which you patiently endured. And excellent is the final home."﴾ It was said: they are secure therein. The implied sense is: and they say, "Peace be upon you."

Muqatil said: they enter, within the span of a day and night of the days of this world, three times, bringing gifts and presents, saying: "Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured."

From Salih, from Yazid, from Anas ibn Malik: that he recited this verse, "Gardens of perpetual residence" up to His words, "excellent is the final home."

Then he said: It is a Paradise of gold and silver, its height in the air is sixty miles, with no crack or joint in it. Each corner of it has its people. It has four thousand leaves of gold, and at each door stand seventy thousand angels, and with each angel is a gift from the Most Merciful, the like of which does not exist. [.........] [[An unreadable word.]] there is no veil between them and Him.

Ibn al-Mubarak narrated from 'Uqba ibn al-Walid, who said: Artat ibn al-Mundhir told us: I heard a man from Mulajlaj bi-al-Jund, called Abu al-Hajjaj, say: My maternal uncle, Abu Umama, told me: "Indeed the believer, when he enters Paradise, reclines on his couch, and at his side are two rows of servants, and at the end of the two rows is a wall. An angel comes and asks permission. The one nearest to him says: 'An angel asks permission,' and the one next to him says: 'An angel asks permission,' and so on until it reaches the believer, who says: 'Let him in.' The one nearest to the believer says: 'Let him in,' and the one next to him says the same to the one beside him, until it reaches the farthest of them at the door. It is opened for him, and he enters, greets, and then departs." [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 13/186.]]

From 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do you know who will be the first of Allah's creation to enter Paradise?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "The poor and the emigrants, through whom the frontiers are guarded and hardships are averted, and one of them dies with a need in his heart that he cannot fulfill." [145] [[Musnad Ahmad: 2/168.]]

He said: Then the angels come to them: ﴿They enter upon them from every gate, saying: "Peace be upon you, for that which you patiently endured."﴾

Sahl ibn Abi Salih narrated from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) used to visit the graves of the martyrs at the beginning of every year, saying: "Peace be upon you for that which you patiently endured; and excellent is the final home."

Abu Bakr, 'Umar and 'Uthman (peace be upon them) used to do the same.

﴿And those who break the covenant of Allah after its ratification, and sever what Allah has commanded to be joined, and cause corruption in the earth, for them is the curse, and for them is the evil abode﴾, meaning the Fire.

Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas said: "They are the Harurites (Kharijites)."

﴿Allah extends provision to whom He wills, and restricts it﴾, meaning He widens it for whom He wills, ﴿and constricts﴾ and straitens. ﴿And they rejoiced in the life of this world﴾, meaning they neglected and were ignorant of what is with Allah, and they coveted. ﴿And the life of this world, in the Hereafter, is but a little enjoyment﴾, a small and passing thing. This was said by Mujahid. 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabit said: "Like the provision of a shepherd who takes with him a handful of dates, or some flour, or something over which he drinks milk." [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 13/189.]]

al-Kalbi said: "Like a small bowl, a dish, a cup, a pot, and the like, from which one benefits and then it passes away."

﴿And those who disbelieve, from the people of Makkah, say: "Why has a sign not been sent down upon him from his Lord?"﴾ Say: ﴿Indeed, Allah misguides whom He wills and guides to Himself whoever turns back﴾, guiding the community to His obedience, the one who returns to Him with his heart. Then He described them, saying: ﴿Those who believe﴾ in the place of accusative, and the preceding "alladhina" is in the nominative. ﴿And their hearts find rest in the remembrance of Allah.﴾

Muqatil said: "With the Qur'an." ﴿Unquestionably, by the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest.﴾

Ibn 'Abbas said: "This is about oaths: when a Muslim swears by Allah about something, that is what calms the hearts of the believers toward it."

Mujahid said: "They are the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)."

﴿Those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them is Tuba (bliss)﴾, a beginning, and its predicate follows. It was said: its meaning is "for them is Tuba," so "Tuba" is the predicate of the first subject.

The scholars differed in interpreting "Tuba."

al-Walibi reported from Ibn 'Abbas: "Tuba lahum": joy and comfort of the eye for them. 'Ikrima said: "How good is what they have." al-Dahhak said: "Enviable state for them." Qatada said: "Beautiful state for them." Ma'mar reported from him: "This is an Arabic expression; a man says to another, 'Tuba lakum,' meaning you have obtained good." Ibrahim said: "Goodness and honor for them." Shumayt ibn 'Ajlan said: "Tuba means the continuance of good." al-Farra' said: "It derives from goodness, and the waw came because of the preceding damma, and it is from the speech of the Arabs: 'Tubaka, tuba laka.'" Sa'id ibn Jubayr reported from Ibn 'Abbas: "Tuba is the name of Paradise in Abyssinian." Sa'id ibn Masjuh said: "It is the name of Paradise in Hindi; the 'spring of the garden' in the language of India." [[Cf. Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 2/53.]]

Ibn Sa'id al-Hindi narrated from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that a man said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, what is Tuba?" He said: "A tree in Paradise, whose length is a hundred years; the garments of the people of Paradise come out of its sheaths." [146] [[Musnad Ahmad: 3/71.]]

Mu'awiya ibn Murra narrated from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Tuba is a tree which Allah planted with His hand and breathed into it of His spirit. It brings forth ornaments and garments, and its branches can be seen from beyond the wall of Paradise." [147] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 14/357, no. 39250.]]

Abu Hurayra said: "Tuba is a tree in Paradise, which Allah planted for it; its fruit ... for My servant 'Ayyash, prepared for him from ornaments, with its saddle and its flesh, and from camels, beneath which is cloth of garments."

Mughith ibn Sumayy said: "Tuba is a tree of Paradise. If a man rode a young she-camel and then went around with her, he would not reach the place from which he set out until he died of old age. There is not a household but has in it a branch of that tree hanging down, the water reaching them by buckets. When they wish to eat from the fruit, it lowers itself to them, and they eat from it what they wish. Birds like camels come upon it, and they eat from it roasted and cooked meat, and then they fly off." [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 13/195.]]

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 13, verse 15–29 (part 2 of 2):

Qal ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr: hiya shajara fi Jannat ʿAdn, asluha fi dar al-Nabi ﷺ, wa fi kull dar wa ghurfa ghusn minha. Lam yakhluq Allah lawnan wa la zahra illa wa fiha minha, illa al-sawad, wa lam yakhluq Allah fakiha wa la thamara illa wa fiha minha. Yanbaʿu min asliha ʿaynan: al-Kafur wa al-Salsabil. Muqabil kull waraqa minha tuzallu umma ʿalayha, ʿalayha malak yusabbihu Allah bi-anwaʿ al-tasbih. [[Al-ʿUmda ʿan al-Tha'labi: 351, wa Fath al-Qadir: 4/373 ḥ 5312.]]

Wa qal Abu Salam: ḥaddathani ʿAmir ibn Zayd al-Bakali annahu samiʿa ʿUtba ibn ʿUbayd al-Sulami yaqulu: jaʾa aʿrabi ila al-Nabi ﷺ fa-qal: "Ya Rasul Allah, fi al-Janna fakiha?" Qal: "Fiha shajara tudʿa Tuba, hiya tutabiqu al-Firdaws." [[Al-Muʿjam al-Kabir: 17/127, Jamiʿ al-Bayan li-l-Tabari: 13/195.]]

Qal: "Ayy shajar ardina tushabih?" Qal: "Laysa tushabihu shayʾan min shajar ardika, wa lakin atayta al-Sham." Faqal: "Atayta al-Sham ya Rasul Allah ﷺ?" Qal: "Fa-innaha tushabihu shajara tudʿa al-Jawz, tanbutu ʿala saqin wahid thumma yantashiru aʿlaha." Faqal: "Ma aʿzama asliha!"

Qal: "Law irtahalat jadʿa min ibil ahlika ma ahatat bi-asliha hatta tankasira tarquwatahuma harman." [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 13/195.]]

Qal Wahb ibn Munabbih: inna fi al-Jannati shajara. Qal: al-Tuba yasiru al-rakib fi zillaha miʾata ʿam wa la yaqtaʿuha. Zahruha riyat, wa waraquha burud, wa qidabuha ʿanbar, wa baṭḥaʾuha yaqut, wa turabuha kafur, wa ḥamluha misk, yakhruju min asliha anhar al-khamr wa al-laban wa al-ʿasal. Wa hiya majlis li-ahl al-Jannah, fa-baynama hum fi majlisihim idha atathum al-malaʾika min rabbihim yaqudun lijamaha, mazmuma bi-salasil min dhahab, wujuhuha ka-l-masabih husnan, wa wabruha ka-khazz al-marʿazi min layyina, ʿalayha rihal alwahuha min yaqut wa dafufuha min dhahab wa thiyabuha min sundusin wa istabraq. Fa-yaftaḥunaha wa yaqulun: inna rabbana arsalana ilaykum li-tazuruhu wa tusallimu ʿalayhi.

Qal: Fa-yarkabunaha fa-hiya asraʿu min al-ṭaʾir wa awṭaʾu min al-firash, najaban min ghayr mahna. Yasiru al-rajul ila janb akhihi wa huwa yukallimuhu wa yunajihi, la tuṣibu udhnu rahila minha idhna ṣāḥibatiha. Ḥatta inna al-shajara li-tantahi ʿan ṭuruqihim, fa-hum la yufarriquna bayn al-rajul wa bayn akhihi. Qal: Fa-yatuna ila al-Rahman al-Rahim fa-yusfiru lahum ʿan wajhihi al-karim, ḥatta yanẓuru ilayhi. Fa-idha ra'awhu qalu: "Allahumma anta al-Salam wa minka al-Salam, wa anta al-Jalal wa al-Ikram." Wa yaqulu tabaraka wa taʿala ʿinda dhalika: "Ana al-Salam wa minni al-Salam, wa ʿalaykum ḥaqqat raḥmati wa maḥabbati. Marḥaban bi-ʿibadi alladhina khashawni bi-l-ghayb wa aṭaʿu amri." Qal: Fa-yaqulun: "Rabbana lam naʿbudka ḥaqqa ʿibadatika wa lam naqdirka ḥaqqa qadrika, fa-adhan lana fi al-sujud qudamaka." Qal: Fa-yaqulu Allah ʿazza wa jalla: "Innaha laysat bi-dar nasab wa ʿibada, wa lakinna dar mulk wa naʿim, wa inni qad rafaʿtu ʿankum nasab al-ʿibada, fa-salūnī ma shi'tum, fa-inna li-kull rajul minkum umniyatahu." Fa-yasʾaluhu ḥatta inna aqṣarahum umniyatan yaqulu: "Rabbi, yatanafasu ahl al-dunya fi dunyahum fa-taḍayaqū fīha, fa-ataniya mithl kull shayʾin kanu fihi min yawm khalaqtaha ila an intahat." Fa-yaqulu Allah ʿazza wa jalla: "Laqad qaṣarat bika umniyatuka, wa laqad saʾalta dūna manzilatika, hadha laka minni, wa sa-alḥiquka bi-man ata, li-annahu laysa fi ʿaṭāʾī takdīr wa la taṣdīr."

Qal: Thumma yaqulu: "Aʿriḍū ʿalā ʿibadī mā lam tablugh umniyatuhum wa lam yakhṭur lahum ʿalā bāl," fa-yaʿriḍūna ʿalayhim ḥatta taqṣura bihim amāniyyuhum allatī fī anfusihim, fa-yakūnu fīmā yaʿriḍūna ʿalayhim barādhīn muqarrana ʿalā kull arbaʿa minhum sarīr min yāqūta wāḥida, ʿalā kull sarīr minhā qubba min dhahab mufraghah. Fī kull qubba minhā furush min furush al-Jannah muẓāhara, fī kull qubba minhā jāriyatān min al-Ḥūr al-ʿĪn, wa ʿalā kull jāriya minhunna thawbān min thiyāb al-Jannah. Wa laysa fi al-Jannati lawn illa wa huwa fīhimā, wa lā rīḥ ṭayyib illā wa qad ʿabiqa bihimā. Yanfudhu ḍawʾ wujūhihimā ghilaẓ al-qubba ḥatta yaẓunnu man yarāhumā annahumā dūna al-qubba, yurā mukhhumā min fawq saqfihimā, ka-l-silk al-abyaḍ min yāqūta ḥamrāʾ.

Yarayāni lahu min al-faḍl ʿalā ṣāḥibatihi ka-faḍl al-shams ʿalā al-ḥijāra aw afḍal, wa yarā huwa lahumā mithl dhalika. Thumma yadkhulu ilayhimā fa-yuṭayyibānihi wa yuqabbilānihi wa yuʿāniqānihi, wa yaqūlāni lahu: "Wallahi ma ẓanannā anna Allah yakhluqu mithlaka." [[Fī al-maṣdar: fa-yuḥayyiyānihi wa yuqabbilānihi wa yatarallaqāni bihi.]] Thumma yaʾmuru Allah al-malaʾika fayasīrūna bihim ṣaffan fī al-Jannah ḥatta yantahiya kull rajul minhum ila manzilatihi allatī uʿiddat lahu. [[Bi-ṭūlihi fī Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 3/533, wa Tafsir al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/60.]]

Al-Kalbi ʿan Abi Salih ʿan Ibn ʿAbbas: "Fa-Ṭūbā lahum" shajara aslaha fi dar ʿAlī fi al-Jannah, wa fi dar kull mu'min minha ghusn yuqalu lahu Ṭūbā.

"Wa ḥusnu maʾab": ḥusnu al-marjiʿ.

Wa rawā Dawud ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbar ʿan Jabir ʿan Abi Jaʿfar qal: su'ila Rasul Allah ﷺ ʿan qawlihi "Ṭūbā lahum wa ḥusnu maʾab." Faqal: "Shajara aslaha fi dari wa farʿuha fi al-Jannah." Thumma su'ila ʿanha marratan ukhra, faqal: "Shajara fi al-Jannah aslaha fi dar ʿAlī wa farʿuha ʿala ahl al-Jannah." Faqila lahu: "Ya Rasul Allah, nas'aluka ʿanha marra, faqulta: 'Shajara fi al-Jannah aslaha fi dar ʿAlī wa farʿuha ʿala ahl al-Jannah'," faqal: "Dhalika fi dari wa dar ʿAlī aydan wahida fi makan wahid." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 9/317, wa al-ʿUmda ʿan al-Tha'labi: 351.]]

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 13, verses 15–29 (part 1 of 2):

﴿And to Allah prostrate whoever is in the heavens and the earth,﴾ meaning the angels and the believers, ﴿willingly and unwillingly﴾ meaning the hypocrites and the disbelievers who were compelled to prostrate with the sword.

Ibn al-Mubarak narrated from Sufyan, who said: "Rabi' ibn Hushaym, whenever he recited this verse, would say: 'Nay, willingly, O my Lord!'"

﴿and their shadows at morning and evening﴾ meaning the shadows of those who prostrate, willingly or unwillingly. Their shadow prostrates to Allah when it inclines from their right or left.

Ibn 'Abbas said: "Its parallel is in al-Nahl (surah 16)."

al-Kalbi said: "When he prostrates at morning or evening, his shadow prostrates with him."

Mujahid said: "The shadow of the believer prostrates willingly, as he is obedient, and the shadow of the disbeliever prostrates willingly while he is unwilling." ﴿al-asal﴾ is the plural of ﴿asil﴾, and ﴿al-asil﴾ is the period from the afternoon ('asr) until sunset.

﴿Say: Who is the Lord of the heavens and the earth?﴾ That is, their Creator and Manager. ﴿They will say: "Allah."﴾ They have no choice but to say this. When they answer you, ﴿say: "You too, say, Allah."﴾ Then, as a binding argument against them, it is said: ﴿Have you then taken, besides Him, protectors who do not possess for themselves any benefit or harm?﴾ meaning idols that they worship besides Allah, and which cannot possess for themselves any benefit or harm. Then the matter is put to them in another way: ﴿Say: Are the blind and the seeing equal?﴾ Likewise, the one who has strayed and the believer who is guided are not equal.

al-A'mash, 'Asim, Hamza and al-Kisa'i recited ﴿Am hal yastawi al-zulumat wa al-nur﴾ with the verb in the masculine (yastawi). The rest recited it with the feminine (tastawi). Abu 'Ubayd preferred this, saying: "Because it is joined to a feminine noun, and the verb is closer to the subject, and ﴿al-zulumat wa al-nur﴾ are like disbelief and faith."

﴿Or have they set up for Allah partners who created as He creates, so that the creation seemed similar to them?﴾ So they became unable to tell whether it was the creation of Allah or the creation of their gods. ﴿Say: Allah is the Creator of all things, and He is the One, the Subduer.﴾ [.........] [[An unreadable word.]] for truth and falsehood, two examples. Then the Mighty and Majestic One said: ﴿He sends down from the sky﴾ meaning rain, ﴿water, and valleys flow according to their measure﴾ large according to its measure and small according to its measure. ﴿So the torrent carries a foaming scum﴾ that arose from that flood, ﴿rising to the surface﴾ as the water is heated. The water that remains, pure and beneficial, is the truth. The scum that departs and vanishes, which clings to trees and the sides of valleys and rivers, is the falsehood. It is said: this is the flood of the Qur'an, which descends from the sky, and the hearts take from it their share according to their certainty and doubt, reason and ignorance. So this is the parable of truth and falsehood. [[Zad al-Masir: 4/237.]]

The other parable is His words: ﴿And from that which they kindle in the fire﴾.

Hamid Abu Mihjan, Abu Wahb and Hamza and al-Kisa'i recited ﴿yuqidun﴾ with the verb in the third person (yu-). Abu 'Ubayd preferred this, because of His words ﴿what benefits people﴾, and there is no address here. ﴿Seeking ornaments﴾ meaning adornment they make, ﴿or goods﴾ meaning what is benefited from; and everything one enjoys is a ﴿mata'﴾ (enjoyment).

al-Mash'ath said:
"Enjoy yourself, O Mash'ath, for whatever
you have been given before death is the enjoyment."
[[Tafsir al-Tabari: 13/180; Taj al-'Arus: 5/507.]]

By this he meant the precious things of the earth, gold and silver, ﴿iron, brass, copper and lead﴾, and from them one extracts things that benefit, such as ornaments, vessels and others.

﴿A scum like it.﴾ He says: it has a scum, when the feminine is used, like the scum of the flood. What remains pure from these precious things is what remains, and its dross departs, and the scum that does not remain and is not beneficial is like falsehood.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Thus Allah sets forth truth and falsehood. As for the scum, it passes away as worthless.﴾ ﴿Then the scum that rose over the flood will depart as foam, scattered quickly.﴾ Abu 'Amr said: it comes from the saying of the Arabs: "ajfa'at al-qidr al-nidhr wa jannat," which means when it boils and its scum overflows, or when it settles, nothing of it remains. [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 13/180.]]

al-Qutabi said: "al-jifa' is what the valley throws out to its banks." Then he said: "jafa'tuhu" means "I knocked him down."

Ibn al-Anbari said: "jifa'" means "scattered, perished."

It is said: "jafa'at al-rih bi al-ghaym" when the wind scatters the clouds and carries them away.

Some of them said: it means the earth's separation. It is said: "jafa'a al-wadi" and "ajfa'a" when it dried up.

al-Farra' said: "He only meant by His words jufa'an (as foam) the jifa', because it is a verbal noun. Your saying: 'jafa'a al-wadi ghathauhu jifa'an' (the valley cast out its scum as foam) came out in the form of a noun, though it is a verbal noun." The Arabs do the same with the verbal noun of every verb where a thing gathers part to part, such as ﴿qamash﴾ (miscellany), ﴿raqaq﴾ (rags), ﴿hutam﴾ (debris) and ﴿ghunam﴾ (spoils); they bring it out in the manner of a noun, as in their saying: "a'taytuhu 'ata'an" in the sense of "i'ta'" (giving). Had they intended the verbal noun in its proper form for qamash, they would say: "qammashtuhu qamashan."

﴿As for that which benefits people, it remains in the earth.﴾ ﴿Thus Allah sets forth the parables.﴾ The speech on this is complete. Then He said: ﴿For those who responded to their Lord, the best reward.﴾ That is, obeyed Him: the good in Paradise. ﴿And those who did not respond to Him, even if they had all that is in the earth and the like of it with it, they would surely offer it as ransom on the Day of Resurrection.﴾ Allah said: ﴿For those is the evil reckoning﴾, requiting them with punishment. Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said, and the scum: "Do you know what the evil reckoning is?"
I said: "No."
He said: "It is that a man is called to account for a sin he committed, and his sin is not forgiven."

﴿And their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the resting place﴾ meaning the bed and the destination.

﴿Is then one who knows that what has been sent down to you from your Lord is the truth [.........] [[An unreadable word.]]﴾ so he is sufficient, ﴿like one who is blind to it﴾, who does not know it and does not act upon it? ﴿Only those of understanding remember﴾. The address is to the companions and the people of reason, ﴿who fulfill the covenant of Allah﴾ in their affairs, meaning His obligation upon them, so they do not oppose it for that in which they are, ﴿and do not break the pact﴾, ﴿and those who join what Allah has commanded to be joined﴾. It was said: He meant faith in all the books and messengers, and they do not disbelieve in them.

Most of the exegetes said: it means the kinship ties (rahm), and they sever them.

al-Zuhri, from Abu Salama ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, said: "Abu al-Darda' fell ill, and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf visited him. He said: 'Choose for them the one who joins them, as far as you know, O Muhammad.' 'Abd al-Rahman said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Allah, blessed and exalted, said: I am Allah and I am the Merciful. I created the womb and derived for it a name from My name. Whoever joins it, I join him, and whoever severs it, I sever him.'" [141] [[Musnad Ahmad: 1/194, where it reads "battatahu" in place of "qata'atahu"; the full text is in Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 1/104.]]

From Shayba, who said: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Mawhab and his father 'Uthman ibn 'Abd Allah told us that they both heard Musa ibn Talha narrate from Abu Ayyub al-Ansari: that a man said: "O Messenger of Allah, inform me of a deed that will admit me to Paradise." The people said: "What is wrong with him? What is wrong with him?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "He has a need." Then the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "You worship Allah, associating nothing with Him, establish the prayer, give the zakat, and join the ties of kinship, leave it." He said: as if he was on his mount. [142] [[Sahih Ibn Hibban: 8/38.]]

From 'Ata' ibn Abi Marwan, from his father, from Ka'b, who said: "By the One who split the sea for the Children of Israel, indeed in the Torah it is written: 'O son of Adam, fear your Lord, be dutiful to your parents, join your kinship ties; I will lengthen your life for you, make your ease easy for you, and turn away your hardship from you.'" [[Al-Musannaf of Ibn Abi Shayba: 6/97.]]

And from Abu Ishaq, from Mughra' al-'Abdi, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: "Whoever fears his Lord and joins his kinship ties, his life will be extended, his wealth will increase, and his family will love him." [[Al-Adab al-Mufrad: 24.]]

From Salih, from Jarir, from Burd, from Makhul, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do good [there is no act of obedience to Allah more quickly rewarded than joining kinship ties], and there is nothing more quickly punished than oppression and severing kinship ties, and a false oath leaves homes desolate." [143] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 3/368; al-Jami' al-Saghir: 2/455.]]

﴿And those who are patient﴾ in obedience to Allah and restrain themselves from disobedience to Allah. This was said by Ibn Zayd. Ibn 'Abbas said: "And they were patient in the command of Allah." 'Ata' said: "In calamities, misfortunes, accidents and trials." Abu 'Imran al-Juni said: "They were patient in their religion."

﴿Seeking the face of Allah﴾, a seeker who holds fast to Allah and asks his Lord for forgiveness that he might disobey Him or oppose His command, ﴿and establish the prayer, and spend of what We have provided them, secretly and openly﴾, meaning the zakat. ﴿And they repel with good the evil﴾ meaning they push it away. It is said: "daraa Allah 'anni bi-sharrika" (Allah has warded off your evil from me).

Ibn Zayd said: that is, they do not repay evil with evil, but repel it with good.

al-Qutabi said: its meaning is that when they are insulted, they show forbearance; the insult is the evil and the forbearance is the good.

Qatada said: they return kindness to those who wrong them. Its parallel is: ﴿When the ignorant address them, they say, "Peace."﴾ [[Surat al-Furqan: 63.]]

al-Hasan said: when they are denied, they give; when they are wronged, they pardon; and when they are severed, they join.

Ibn Kaysan said: when they sin, they despair; and when they transgress, they are rewarded, so that by repentance they ward off from themselves, and the sin is forgiven.

This is the statement of Ibn 'Abbas in the narration of al-Dahhak from him, who said: "They repel evil deeds with righteous deeds." This is supported by the reported hadith: Mu'adh ibn Jabal said: "O Messenger of Allah, advise me." He said: "When you do an evil deed, follow it with a good deed to erase it: secret with secret, and open with open." [144] [[Majma' al-Zawa'id: 4/218.]]

'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak said: "These are eight qualities, indicating the eight gates of Paradise."

Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: "These are eight bridges; whoever wishes nearness to Allah must cross them." [[Tafsir al-Tha'alibi: 3/367.]]

﴿Those will have the good final home﴾. Then He explained, saying: ﴿Gardens of perpetual residence which they will enter.﴾

The common readers recited it with a fatha on the ya' and a damma on the kha' (yadkhulunaha). Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr recited it with a damma on the ya' and a fatha on the kha' (yudkhalunaha).

'Abd Allah ibn 'Umayr said: "In Paradise there is a palace called 'Adn, around which are towers and meadows. It has five thousand doors, and at each door are five thousand brides. Only a prophet, a truthful one, or a martyr enters it." [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 15/834; Tafsir al-Tabari: 10/232.]] [[In al-Tabari: "al-rawh" (the meadows); in Majma' al-Zawa'id (5/196): "al-suruh" (the palaces).]]

﴿And whoever is righteous among their fathers, their spouses and their offspring﴾, meaning their families and children also, will enter it. ﴿And the angels will enter upon them from every gate, saying: "Peace be upon you, for that which you patiently endured. And excellent is the final home."﴾ It was said: they are secure therein. The implied sense is: and they say, "Peace be upon you."

Muqatil said: they enter, within the span of a day and night of the days of this world, three times, bringing gifts and presents, saying: "Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured."

From Salih, from Yazid, from Anas ibn Malik: that he recited this verse, "Gardens of perpetual residence" up to His words, "excellent is the final home."

Then he said: It is a Paradise of gold and silver, its height in the air is sixty miles, with no crack or joint in it. Each corner of it has its people. It has four thousand leaves of gold, and at each door stand seventy thousand angels, and with each angel is a gift from the Most Merciful, the like of which does not exist. [.........] [[An unreadable word.]] there is no veil between them and Him.

Ibn al-Mubarak narrated from 'Uqba ibn al-Walid, who said: Artat ibn al-Mundhir told us: I heard a man from Mulajlaj bi-al-Jund, called Abu al-Hajjaj, say: My maternal uncle, Abu Umama, told me: "Indeed the believer, when he enters Paradise, reclines on his couch, and at his side are two rows of servants, and at the end of the two rows is a wall. An angel comes and asks permission. The one nearest to him says: 'An angel asks permission,' and the one next to him says: 'An angel asks permission,' and so on until it reaches the believer, who says: 'Let him in.' The one nearest to the believer says: 'Let him in,' and the one next to him says the same to the one beside him, until it reaches the farthest of them at the door. It is opened for him, and he enters, greets, and then departs." [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 13/186.]]

From 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do you know who will be the first of Allah's creation to enter Paradise?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "The poor and the emigrants, through whom the frontiers are guarded and hardships are averted, and one of them dies with a need in his heart that he cannot fulfill." [145] [[Musnad Ahmad: 2/168.]]

He said: Then the angels come to them: ﴿They enter upon them from every gate, saying: "Peace be upon you, for that which you patiently endured."﴾

Sahl ibn Abi Salih narrated from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) used to visit the graves of the martyrs at the beginning of every year, saying: "Peace be upon you for that which you patiently endured; and excellent is the final home."

Abu Bakr, 'Umar and 'Uthman (peace be upon them) used to do the same.

﴿And those who break the covenant of Allah after its ratification, and sever what Allah has commanded to be joined, and cause corruption in the earth, for them is the curse, and for them is the evil abode﴾, meaning the Fire.

Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas said: "They are the Harurites (Kharijites)."

﴿Allah extends provision to whom He wills, and restricts it﴾, meaning He widens it for whom He wills, ﴿and constricts﴾ and straitens. ﴿And they rejoiced in the life of this world﴾, meaning they neglected and were ignorant of what is with Allah, and they coveted. ﴿And the life of this world, in the Hereafter, is but a little enjoyment﴾, a small and passing thing. This was said by Mujahid. 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabit said: "Like the provision of a shepherd who takes with him a handful of dates, or some flour, or something over which he drinks milk." [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 13/189.]]

al-Kalbi said: "Like a small bowl, a dish, a cup, a pot, and the like, from which one benefits and then it passes away."

﴿And those who disbelieve, from the people of Makkah, say: "Why has a sign not been sent down upon him from his Lord?"﴾ Say: ﴿Indeed, Allah misguides whom He wills and guides to Himself whoever turns back﴾, guiding the community to His obedience, the one who returns to Him with his heart. Then He described them, saying: ﴿Those who believe﴾ in the place of accusative, and the preceding "alladhina" is in the nominative. ﴿And their hearts find rest in the remembrance of Allah.﴾

Muqatil said: "With the Qur'an." ﴿Unquestionably, by the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest.﴾

Ibn 'Abbas said: "This is about oaths: when a Muslim swears by Allah about something, that is what calms the hearts of the believers toward it."

Mujahid said: "They are the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)."

﴿Those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them is Tuba (bliss)﴾, a beginning, and its predicate follows. It was said: its meaning is "for them is Tuba," so "Tuba" is the predicate of the first subject.

The scholars differed in interpreting "Tuba."

al-Walibi reported from Ibn 'Abbas: "Tuba lahum": joy and comfort of the eye for them. 'Ikrima said: "How good is what they have." al-Dahhak said: "Enviable state for them." Qatada said: "Beautiful state for them." Ma'mar reported from him: "This is an Arabic expression; a man says to another, 'Tuba lakum,' meaning you have obtained good." Ibrahim said: "Goodness and honor for them." Shumayt ibn 'Ajlan said: "Tuba means the continuance of good." al-Farra' said: "It derives from goodness, and the waw came because of the preceding damma, and it is from the speech of the Arabs: 'Tubaka, tuba laka.'" Sa'id ibn Jubayr reported from Ibn 'Abbas: "Tuba is the name of Paradise in Abyssinian." Sa'id ibn Masjuh said: "It is the name of Paradise in Hindi; the 'spring of the garden' in the language of India." [[Cf. Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 2/53.]]

Ibn Sa'id al-Hindi narrated from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that a man said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, what is Tuba?" He said: "A tree in Paradise, whose length is a hundred years; the garments of the people of Paradise come out of its sheaths." [146] [[Musnad Ahmad: 3/71.]]

Mu'awiya ibn Murra narrated from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Tuba is a tree which Allah planted with His hand and breathed into it of His spirit. It brings forth ornaments and garments, and its branches can be seen from beyond the wall of Paradise." [147] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 14/357, no. 39250.]]

Abu Hurayra said: "Tuba is a tree in Paradise, which Allah planted for it; its fruit ... for My servant 'Ayyash, prepared for him from ornaments, with its saddle and its flesh, and from camels, beneath which is cloth of garments."

Mughith ibn Sumayy said: "Tuba is a tree of Paradise. If a man rode a young she-camel and then went around with her, he would not reach the place from which he set out until he died of old age. There is not a household but has in it a branch of that tree hanging down, the water reaching them by buckets. When they wish to eat from the fruit, it lowers itself to them, and they eat from it what they wish. Birds like camels come upon it, and they eat from it roasted and cooked meat, and then they fly off." [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 13/195.]]

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 13, verse 15–29 (part 2 of 2):

Qal ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr: hiya shajara fi Jannat ʿAdn, asluha fi dar al-Nabi ﷺ, wa fi kull dar wa ghurfa ghusn minha. Lam yakhluq Allah lawnan wa la zahra illa wa fiha minha, illa al-sawad, wa lam yakhluq Allah fakiha wa la thamara illa wa fiha minha. Yanbaʿu min asliha ʿaynan: al-Kafur wa al-Salsabil. Muqabil kull waraqa minha tuzallu umma ʿalayha, ʿalayha malak yusabbihu Allah bi-anwaʿ al-tasbih. [[Al-ʿUmda ʿan al-Tha'labi: 351, wa Fath al-Qadir: 4/373 ḥ 5312.]]

Wa qal Abu Salam: ḥaddathani ʿAmir ibn Zayd al-Bakali annahu samiʿa ʿUtba ibn ʿUbayd al-Sulami yaqulu: jaʾa aʿrabi ila al-Nabi ﷺ fa-qal: "Ya Rasul Allah, fi al-Janna fakiha?" Qal: "Fiha shajara tudʿa Tuba, hiya tutabiqu al-Firdaws." [[Al-Muʿjam al-Kabir: 17/127, Jamiʿ al-Bayan li-l-Tabari: 13/195.]]

Qal: "Ayy shajar ardina tushabih?" Qal: "Laysa tushabihu shayʾan min shajar ardika, wa lakin atayta al-Sham." Faqal: "Atayta al-Sham ya Rasul Allah ﷺ?" Qal: "Fa-innaha tushabihu shajara tudʿa al-Jawz, tanbutu ʿala saqin wahid thumma yantashiru aʿlaha." Faqal: "Ma aʿzama asliha!"

Qal: "Law irtahalat jadʿa min ibil ahlika ma ahatat bi-asliha hatta tankasira tarquwatahuma harman." [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 13/195.]]

Qal Wahb ibn Munabbih: inna fi al-Jannati shajara. Qal: al-Tuba yasiru al-rakib fi zillaha miʾata ʿam wa la yaqtaʿuha. Zahruha riyat, wa waraquha burud, wa qidabuha ʿanbar, wa baṭḥaʾuha yaqut, wa turabuha kafur, wa ḥamluha misk, yakhruju min asliha anhar al-khamr wa al-laban wa al-ʿasal. Wa hiya majlis li-ahl al-Jannah, fa-baynama hum fi majlisihim idha atathum al-malaʾika min rabbihim yaqudun lijamaha, mazmuma bi-salasil min dhahab, wujuhuha ka-l-masabih husnan, wa wabruha ka-khazz al-marʿazi min layyina, ʿalayha rihal alwahuha min yaqut wa dafufuha min dhahab wa thiyabuha min sundusin wa istabraq. Fa-yaftaḥunaha wa yaqulun: inna rabbana arsalana ilaykum li-tazuruhu wa tusallimu ʿalayhi.

Qal: Fa-yarkabunaha fa-hiya asraʿu min al-ṭaʾir wa awṭaʾu min al-firash, najaban min ghayr mahna. Yasiru al-rajul ila janb akhihi wa huwa yukallimuhu wa yunajihi, la tuṣibu udhnu rahila minha idhna ṣāḥibatiha. Ḥatta inna al-shajara li-tantahi ʿan ṭuruqihim, fa-hum la yufarriquna bayn al-rajul wa bayn akhihi. Qal: Fa-yatuna ila al-Rahman al-Rahim fa-yusfiru lahum ʿan wajhihi al-karim, ḥatta yanẓuru ilayhi. Fa-idha ra'awhu qalu: "Allahumma anta al-Salam wa minka al-Salam, wa anta al-Jalal wa al-Ikram." Wa yaqulu tabaraka wa taʿala ʿinda dhalika: "Ana al-Salam wa minni al-Salam, wa ʿalaykum ḥaqqat raḥmati wa maḥabbati. Marḥaban bi-ʿibadi alladhina khashawni bi-l-ghayb wa aṭaʿu amri." Qal: Fa-yaqulun: "Rabbana lam naʿbudka ḥaqqa ʿibadatika wa lam naqdirka ḥaqqa qadrika, fa-adhan lana fi al-sujud qudamaka." Qal: Fa-yaqulu Allah ʿazza wa jalla: "Innaha laysat bi-dar nasab wa ʿibada, wa lakinna dar mulk wa naʿim, wa inni qad rafaʿtu ʿankum nasab al-ʿibada, fa-salūnī ma shi'tum, fa-inna li-kull rajul minkum umniyatahu." Fa-yasʾaluhu ḥatta inna aqṣarahum umniyatan yaqulu: "Rabbi, yatanafasu ahl al-dunya fi dunyahum fa-taḍayaqū fīha, fa-ataniya mithl kull shayʾin kanu fihi min yawm khalaqtaha ila an intahat." Fa-yaqulu Allah ʿazza wa jalla: "Laqad qaṣarat bika umniyatuka, wa laqad saʾalta dūna manzilatika, hadha laka minni, wa sa-alḥiquka bi-man ata, li-annahu laysa fi ʿaṭāʾī takdīr wa la taṣdīr."

Qal: Thumma yaqulu: "Aʿriḍū ʿalā ʿibadī mā lam tablugh umniyatuhum wa lam yakhṭur lahum ʿalā bāl," fa-yaʿriḍūna ʿalayhim ḥatta taqṣura bihim amāniyyuhum allatī fī anfusihim, fa-yakūnu fīmā yaʿriḍūna ʿalayhim barādhīn muqarrana ʿalā kull arbaʿa minhum sarīr min yāqūta wāḥida, ʿalā kull sarīr minhā qubba min dhahab mufraghah. Fī kull qubba minhā furush min furush al-Jannah muẓāhara, fī kull qubba minhā jāriyatān min al-Ḥūr al-ʿĪn, wa ʿalā kull jāriya minhunna thawbān min thiyāb al-Jannah. Wa laysa fi al-Jannati lawn illa wa huwa fīhimā, wa lā rīḥ ṭayyib illā wa qad ʿabiqa bihimā. Yanfudhu ḍawʾ wujūhihimā ghilaẓ al-qubba ḥatta yaẓunnu man yarāhumā annahumā dūna al-qubba, yurā mukhhumā min fawq saqfihimā, ka-l-silk al-abyaḍ min yāqūta ḥamrāʾ.

Yarayāni lahu min al-faḍl ʿalā ṣāḥibatihi ka-faḍl al-shams ʿalā al-ḥijāra aw afḍal, wa yarā huwa lahumā mithl dhalika. Thumma yadkhulu ilayhimā fa-yuṭayyibānihi wa yuqabbilānihi wa yuʿāniqānihi, wa yaqūlāni lahu: "Wallahi ma ẓanannā anna Allah yakhluqu mithlaka." [[Fī al-maṣdar: fa-yuḥayyiyānihi wa yuqabbilānihi wa yatarallaqāni bihi.]] Thumma yaʾmuru Allah al-malaʾika fayasīrūna bihim ṣaffan fī al-Jannah ḥatta yantahiya kull rajul minhum ila manzilatihi allatī uʿiddat lahu. [[Bi-ṭūlihi fī Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 3/533, wa Tafsir al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/60.]]

Al-Kalbi ʿan Abi Salih ʿan Ibn ʿAbbas: "Fa-Ṭūbā lahum" shajara aslaha fi dar ʿAlī fi al-Jannah, wa fi dar kull mu'min minha ghusn yuqalu lahu Ṭūbā.

"Wa ḥusnu maʾab": ḥusnu al-marjiʿ.

Wa rawā Dawud ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbar ʿan Jabir ʿan Abi Jaʿfar qal: su'ila Rasul Allah ﷺ ʿan qawlihi "Ṭūbā lahum wa ḥusnu maʾab." Faqal: "Shajara aslaha fi dari wa farʿuha fi al-Jannah." Thumma su'ila ʿanha marratan ukhra, faqal: "Shajara fi al-Jannah aslaha fi dar ʿAlī wa farʿuha ʿala ahl al-Jannah." Faqila lahu: "Ya Rasul Allah, nas'aluka ʿanha marra, faqulta: 'Shajara fi al-Jannah aslaha fi dar ʿAlī wa farʿuha ʿala ahl al-Jannah'," faqal: "Dhalika fi dari wa dar ʿAlī aydan wahida fi makan wahid." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 9/317, wa al-ʿUmda ʿan al-Tha'labi: 351.]]

﴿Thus have We sent you, Muhammad, to a community before which other communities have passed away, that you may recite to them what We have revealed to you, while they disbelieve in the Most Merciful﴾ (13:30).

Qatadah, Muqatil and Ibn Juraij said: it was revealed concerning the treaty of al-Hudaybiyah, when they came to the writing of the treaty. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Ali (may Allah be pleased with him): "Write: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate." [150] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 9/317.]]

Suhayl ibn Amr and the polytheists with him said: "We do not know the Most Merciful except the master of Yamamah," meaning Musaylimah the Liar. "Write: In Your name, O Allah," for this is how the people of the Jahiliyyah (Age of Ignorance) used to write.

Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Write: This is what Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, has agreed upon." The polytheists and Quraysh said: "If we knew you were the Messenger of Allah, we would not have fought you or barred you." He said: "Then leave it, but write: This is what Muhammad ibn Abdullah has agreed upon."

The Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Let us fight them." He said: "No, but write as they wish." Then Allah the Exalted revealed this verse concerning them.

Juwaybir narrated from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas, who said: it was revealed concerning the disbelievers of Quraysh when the Prophet (ﷺ) said to them: "Prostrate to the Most Merciful." They said: "And what is the Most Merciful?" So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse.

And He said: Say to them, O Muhammad: ﴿Indeed, the Most Merciful, whose knowledge you deny, is my Lord; there is no god but Him. Upon Him I rely, and to Him is my return﴾ (13:30).

Then comes ﴿And if there had been a Qur'an by which mountains could be set in motion...﴾ (13:31).
