The verse was revealed concerning a group of polytheists of Makkah, among them Abu Jahl ibn Hisham and Abdullah ibn Abi Umayyah al-Makhzumi. The parable of the Garden which the God-fearing have been promised: they disagreed about what makes the subject (*al-mathal*) nominative.

Al-Farra' said: it is a subject (*mubtada'*) and its predicate (*khabar*) is the words ﴿in which rivers flow beneath it﴾ (Qur'an 13:35). It was also said that *al-mathal* means "the description," as in ﴿To Allah belongs the highest description﴾ (Qur'an 16:60), meaning the highest attribute, and ﴿That is their description in the Torah, and their description in the Gospel﴾ (Qur'an 48:29). The meaning of the verse is: the description of the Garden which the God-fearing have been promised is that rivers flow beneath it, and so on and so forth. [Surah al-Nahl: 60. Surah al-Fath: 29.]

It was also said: the *mathal* is ﴿the Garden which the God-fearing have been promised, in which rivers flow beneath it﴾. The Arabs often do this with *mathal* and *mithl*, as in ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾ (Qur'an 42:11), meaning "there is nothing like Him." [Surah al-Shura: 11.]

It was also said that its meaning is: ﴿For those who responded to their Lord is the best (reward)﴾ (Qur'an 13:18). It was said that "the Garden" is a substitute (*badal*) for it. [Surah al-Ra'd: 18.]

Muqatil said: its meaning is that the likeness of the Garden which the God-fearing have been promised, in goodness, blessing and eternity, is like the likeness of the Fire, in punishment, hardship and distress. [The same source: 9/325.]

﴿Its fruit is everlasting and its shade is perpetual﴾. It neither ends nor perishes, and its shade never ceases. This is a refutation of the Jahmiyya (a sect), who said: the bliss of the Garden will perish. ﴿That is the final outcome of those who were God-fearing﴾, meaning the Garden, ﴿and the final outcome of the disbelievers is the Fire﴾.

﴿Those to whom We have given the Book﴾, meaning the Qur'an, and they are the companions of Muhammad, ﴿rejoice at what has been revealed to you﴾ of the Qur'an. ﴿And among the factions﴾, meaning the disbelievers who denied the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), namely the Jews and Christians, ﴿are those who deny part of it﴾. That is because they believed in Surah Yusuf and said that it agreed with their Book. This is the view of Mujahid and Qatada.

The rest of the scholars said: the mention of al-Rahman in the Qur'an was rare at the beginning of what was revealed. When Abdullah ibn Salam and his companions embraced Islam, it grieved them that al-Rahman was seldom mentioned in the Qur'an, because His mention is frequent in the Torah. So they asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about this, and Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Say: Call upon Allah or call upon al-Rahman﴾ (Qur'an 17:110), and the rest of the verse.

When this verse was revealed, the Quraysh said: "What is the matter with Muhammad? He used to call to one God, and today he calls to two gods: Allah and al-Rahman. We do not know al-Rahman except the al-Rahman of Yamama," meaning Musaylima the Liar. So Allah revealed: ﴿And they disbelieve in the Most Merciful when they are reminded of al-Rahman﴾ (Qur'an 13:30). The believers among the People of the Book rejoiced at the mention of al-Rahman, so Allah revealed: ﴿Those to whom We gave the Book rejoice at what has been revealed to you﴾ of the mention of al-Rahman, ﴿and among the factions﴾, meaning the polytheists of Quraysh, ﴿are those who deny part of it﴾. [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 9/326.]

Allah said: Say, O Muhammad: ﴿I have only been commanded to worship Allah and not to associate anything with Him. Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 13, verse 41–43:

Have they not seen that We come to the land, reducing it from its outskirts? (13:41) — meaning the people of Makkah, who ask Muhammad (ﷺ) for faith: that We come to the land, intending it, reducing it from its outskirts, by opening it for Muhammad (ﷺ), land after land around their land, so that they do not fear that We will open their land just as We have opened other than it. The exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil) said something similar to this.

Salih ibn 'Amr narrated from 'Amr ibn 'Ubayd, from al-Hasan, who said: "It is the victory of the Muslims over the polytheists."

Waki' narrated from Salamah ibn Subt, from al-Dahhak, who said: "It is what Muhammad (ﷺ) prevailed over of the enemy's land."

Jubayr narrated from al-Dahhak, who said: "Did the people of Makkah not see that We open for Muhammad what is around him of the villages?"

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Sulami narrated from Muqatil ibn Sulayman, who said: "Al-ard (the land) is Makkah, and nagsuha min atrafiha (reducing it from its outskirts) is the victory of the Prophet (ﷺ) and the believers over it, and their diminishing and the increase of the Muslims. So how do they not take heed!"

And a group said: its meaning is: "Or have they not seen the land that We reduce? Do you not fear that if We bring about such a thing against them and their land, He will destroy them and ruin their land?"

Ibn Abi Najih narrated from Mujahid, who said: "The ruin of the land and the taking of its people."

Yazid al-Khuwayy narrated from 'Ikrimah, who said: "It means the taking of people (qabd al-nas)."

And he said: "If the land were diminished, it would become like this," and he made a gesture with his hands, two parts apart.

'Uthman ibn al-Sanna narrated from al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words nagsuha min atrafiha, he said: "The death of the people of the land."

Talhah ibn Abi Talhah al-Qanad narrated from al-Sha'bi: "The taking of souls and fruits."

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "The decrease of its people and its abandonment."

'Uthman ibn 'Ata narrated from his father, who said: "It is the passing of its scholars and jurists."

'Abd Allah ibn Yusuf ibn Ahmad ibn Babawayh informed us, Abu Raja' Muhammad ibn Hamid ibn Muhammad al-Muqri' in Makkah informed us, Muhammad informed us, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar informed us, Sulayman ibn Arqam informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Salim ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, from his father, that the Prophet (ﷺ) recited it wa min 'indihi 'ulima al-kitab.

And with it, from al-Samari: Abu Tawbah informed us, from al-Kisa'i, from Sulayman, from al-Zuhri, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, who said: He said, and he mentioned that Allah is greater… that when he came to the house to embrace Islam, he heard the Prophet (ﷺ) reciting wa min 'indihi 'ulima al-kitab with kasra on the mim, and he heard him in the second rak'ah reciting bal huwa ayatun bayyinatun fi sudur alladhina (the verse).

Abu Muhammad 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Fasi informed me, al-Qadi al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn 'Uthman al-Nasibi informed us, Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Sumay'i in Aleppo informed us, al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn al-Husayn al-Jassas informed me. al-Husayn ibn al-Hakam informed us, Sa'id ibn 'Uthman informed us, from Abu Maryam; and Ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Ata informed me, saying: I was sitting with Abu Ja'far in the mosque, and I saw the son of 'Abd Allah ibn Salam sitting in a corner. I said to Abu Ja'far: "They claim that the one who has knowledge of the Book is 'Abd Allah ibn Salam." He said: "That is only 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him)."

And in it, from al-Sub'i: 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Mansur ibn al-Junayd al-Razi informed us, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn al-Kitab, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal informed us, Mundal ibn 'Ali informed us, from Isma'il ibn Salman, from Abu 'Umar Zadhan, from Ibn al-Hanafiyyah, regarding wa man 'indahu 'ilmu al-kitab, he said: "It is 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him)" [[Zad al-Masir li-Ibn al-Jawzi: 4/252; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 9/336; Shawahid al-Tanzil: 1/401.]].
